candidates.exact_span: the frequency of testing for this species is automatically increased to once per quarter with no option for frequency reduction.
candidates.computation_change_reason: If the preceding trigger condition is met, this clause establishes a mandatory quarterly testing frequency with no reduction allowed, changing which routine monitoring intervals are applicable for FY2025.

candidates.exact_span: The permittee shall conduct a total of three (3) additional tests for any species that demonstrates significant lethal effects at or below the critical dilution.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of 'significant lethal effects' and whether effects occurred 'at or below the critical dilution' determines both whether a toxicity result exceeds the applicable WET/limit comparison point (A) and whether three additional retests become required rather than optional (B); missing retest evidence is classified differently depending on whether this trigger applied (C).

candidates.exact_span: The three additional tests shall be conducted monthly during the next three consecutive months. If testing on a quarterly basis, the permittee may substitute one of the additional tests in lieu of one routine toxicity test.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Different readings of the monthly schedule versus the quarterly substitution option change how many distinct tests are required in a given period and whether a routine quarterly result can satisfy a retest obligation, affecting monitoring-applicability rows (B) and whether absent data reflects conditional non-requirement versus missing required evidence (C).

candidates.exact_span: A full report shall be prepared for each test required by this section in accordance with the reporting requirements previously outlined and available upon request from the Agency.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether each retest must produce a reportable result, and which external reporting requirements apply, affects whether monitoring was required to be documented and how missing or no-data submissions are evaluated.

candidates.exact_span: If persistent lethality is demonstrated by failure of one or more retests, the permittee shall initiate Toxicity Reduction Evaluation (TRE) requirements as specified in Part 6 of this section.
candidates.computation_change_reason: What counts as 'persistent lethality' and whether 'one or more' failed retests suffice changes when TRE monitoring and follow-up obligations become applicable (B) and whether missing TRE-related evidence reflects a triggered obligation or an unresolved conditional requirement (C).

candidates.exact_span: The permittee shall notify EPA in writing within 5 days of notification of the failure of any retest, and the TRE initiation date will be the test completion date of the first failed retest.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Ambiguity around 'notification of the failure' versus 'test completion date' can change the start of the 5-day notification window and the TRE initiation date used to assess subsequent deadlines.

candidates.exact_span: A TRE may also be required due to a demonstration of intermittent effects at or below the critical dilution, or for failure to perform the required retests.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of 'intermittent effects at or below the critical dilution' affects limit-exceedance assessment for toxicity results (A); 'failure to perform the required retests' creates an independent TRE trigger even without demonstrated lethality (B); absent retest data may be classified as failure to perform required monitoring rather than a documented no-data state (C).

candidates.exact_span: A TRE is triggered following two test failures (a failure followed by one retest failure).
candidates.computation_change_reason: This two-failure formulation can be read differently from the preceding 'failure of one or more retests' language; the chosen interpretation changes when TRE obligations begin and whether missing TRE evidence indicates a triggered requirement or unresolved applicability.

candidates.exact_span: Within ninety (90) days of confirming lethality in the retests, the permittee shall submit a Toxicity Reduction Evaluation (TRE) Action Plan and Schedule for conducting a TRE to the EPA WET Coordinator at 6WQ-PO.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The event that constitutes 'confirming lethality in the retests' sets the 90-day submission deadline; different readings change whether the Action Plan was required by a given FY2025 date and how missing submissions are categorized.

candidates.computation_change_reason: The linkage between TRE outcomes and 'water quality based effluent limits' and 'acceptable level' of toxicity affects how WET-related results are treated as enforceable limit comparisons versus broader compliance objectives.

candidates.exact_span: The TRE Action Plan shall lead to the successful elimination of effluent toxicity at the critical dilution
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of compliance as elimination of toxicity 'at the critical dilution' defines the operative comparison point for whether measured toxicity remains within applicable WET/limit bounds.
